abstract: We present an idea to convert to a unitary quantum walk any open quantum walk which is defined on lattices as well as on finite graphs. This approach generalizes to the domain of open quantum walks (or quantum Markov chains) the framework introduced by Szegedy for quantizing Markov chains. For the unitary quantum walks formulated in this article, we define the probability and the mean probability of finding the walk at a node, then derive the asymptotic mean probability.

specification.problem: Convert an open quantum walk (quantum Markov chain) on a lattice or finite graph into a unitary quantum walk, generalizing Szegedy's quantization of Markov chains. Define the probability and mean probability of finding the walk at a node, and derive the asymptotic mean probability.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the unitary-walk construction and the node probability definitions. The explicit unitary, the OQW Kraus operators, and the asymptotic result are not given in the abstract; only a generic finite-graph instance can be sketched.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: a node-localized state |x0>|c0> on node and auxiliary registers, with rho_0 its density matrix; the actual initial state is not given in the abstract.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state on the node and auxiliary registers.
Apply the unitary walk step U (a Szegedy-type construction built from the OQW transition data; explicit form unknown) t times.
Repeat for t=0..T-1 to build the time-averaged node distribution.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after t applications of U, measure the node register in the computational basis (projectors Pi_x, tracing out the auxiliary register) to sample x with probability P_t(x); repeat over many runs and over t=0..T-1.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_t(x) by outcome frequencies, average over t to get the mean probability (eq_2), and examine the large-T trend to estimate the asymptotic mean probability (eq_3). The paper's analytic derivation of the limit is not given in the abstract.
